key_reasoning.reason: Touches the alembic migration, permission model, assistant share service, assistant router, assistant model (is_shared_with, delete_assistant), assistant repository predicates, generic permission router and PermissionDeletionService, activity repository and activity models, and assistant create/update validation. That is 4+ components across API, service and persistence, with shared utilities (activity repository, permission model) involved. Base is L, bumped to XL for the shared utilities.

The nearest pattern is ActivityRepository.insert, which is fail-open: it is disabled-tolerant and swallows exceptions, and about 14 callers depend on that. A fail-closed, same-transaction variant has no precedent. The server-side personal-integration guard has no backend precedent (the existing rule is UI-only in AssistantSetupSection/AssistantForm). Dropping values_callable changes how the permission enums persist, and datasource app-permission checks share that table. The external-user skip has to land in all three predicate copies. Base is L, bumped to XL because the work is authorization-sensitive.

About 11-13 modified source files (migration, models/permission.py, assistant_share_service.py, routers/assistant.py, models/assistant.py, assistant_repository.py, routers/permission.py, permission_deletion_service.py, activity_repository.py, activity_models.py, the assistant create/update path, possibly ability.py), plus 5 existing test files extended and new tests for the revoke route, permission deletion and the migration. These span the alembic, models, routers, service/assistant, service/permission and service/activity directories.

API (four sharing routes plus the generic permission delete), Service (share, deletion and activity), and DB-Persistence (an enum migration with a downgrade that deletes rows, plus enum mapping changes). The schema change is additive, so it is not significant enough for a further bump.
